name: Pre-Columbian Gold Museum Underground Architectural Tour
description: You will descend into a striking subterranean concrete structure beneath the Plaza de la Cultura to view the world's largest collection of pre-Columbian indigenous gold artifacts. A specialized guide walks you through the spiritual and social significance of these works, dating from 500 AD to 1550 AD. The tour highlights how indigenous metallurgy shaped the cultural identity of the early Isthmus tribes.
location: Plaza de la Cultura, Bajo la Plaza, Calle 5, San José
duration_note: Advance online booking is highly recommended; ticket includes access to the National Coin Museum on the same level.

name: Traditional Gallo Pinto & Coffee Tasting at Mercado Central
description: You will navigate the bustling, century-old maze of the Central Market to pull up a stool at Soda Tapia or Soda Tala. Here, you'll feast on authentic Gallo Pinto (seasoned rice and beans) splashed with local Salsa Lizano, accompanied by sweet plantains and fried cheese. The experience culminates with a traditional 'café chorreado' poured through a wooden stand and cloth filter right before your eyes.
location: Mercado Central, Av. Central, San José
duration_note: Best experienced between 7:00 AM and 10:00 AM for peak morning market energy; cash in local currency is preferred by small sodas.

name: Craft Beer & Tapas Crawl Along Calle 33
description: You will explore the epicenter of Chepe's modern nightlife by hopping between premier craft beer bars like Costa Rica Beer Factory and Wilk Craft Beer in Barrio Escalante. Taste innovative local brews infused with tropical passionfruit or cacao, paired with upscale gastropub chifrijo (layered rice, beans, pork chunks, and pico de gallo). It is a vibrant social scene where you will mingle directly with Josefinos (San José locals).
location: Calle 33, Barrio Escalante, San José
duration_note: Fills up significantly on Thursday through Saturday nights; reservations are advised for larger groups at popular venues.

name: Active Crater Rim Observation & Cloud Forest Walk
description: You will stand right on the edge of a massive, one-mile-wide active volcanic crater to look down at its simmering, sulfuric turquoise acid lake. Afterward, you'll hike through stunted cloud forest vegetation frequently swept by mysterious, fast-moving mists. The high altitude offers crisp air and an otherworldly landscape shaped by historical eruptions.
location: Poás Volcano National Park, Alajuela
duration_note: Strict passport controls and mandatory advanced online ticket purchases required via SINAC portal; viewing depends heavily on morning weather clearings.

name: Class III-IV Whitewater Rafting Through the Pacuare Gorge
description: You will plunge through raging, world-class rapids like 'Huacas' and 'Double Drop' inside an isolated, vertical river canyon blanketed by primary rainforest. Peer up at 300-foot waterfalls cascading directly into the river between heart-pounding stretches of paddling. A riverside deli-style lunch prepared by your river guides on a pristine gravel beach caps off this high-adrenaline day.
location: Pacuare River, Turrialba Operations Base
duration_note: Minimum age is typically 12 years old; physical exertion is high and requiring strong swimming abilities; includes round-trip transport from San José.

name: Artisanal Oxcart Painting Workshop at Fábrica de Carretas Joaquín Chaverri
description: You will immerse yourself in Costa Rica’s deeply rooted rural heritage by visiting a historic 1902 workshop where the country's iconic, brightly painted wooden oxcarts are crafted. Master artisans will teach you the geometric, kaleidoscopic brush strokes that earned these carts a spot on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list. You'll even paint your own small wooden souvenir to take home.
location: Fábrica de Carretas Joaquín Chaverri, Sarchí Norte
duration_note: Great all-weather activity; workshop spaces should be booked 48 hours out during the peak dry season.

name: Historical Architecture Walking Tour of Amón & Otoya Neighborhoods
description: You will stroll past elegant, late 19th-century Victorian and Neo-Mudéjar mansions built by wealthy coffee barons during the golden era of Costa Rican agricultural exports. Your guide reveals hidden architectural details, secret courtyards, and stories of political intrigue that shaped modern Costa Rica. The walk concludes with a fresh tropical juice break in the historic Parque Morazán.
location: Barrio Amón, Av. 7-11, San José
duration_note: Comfortable walking shoes are essential; rain gear is highly recommended if booking an afternoon slot during the green season.

name: Arenal Volcano Lava Flow Hike & Rainforest Trek
description: You will trek across jagged, dramatic black volcanic rock fields left behind by the historic, massive eruption of 1968. As you navigate the trails of Arenal Volcano National Park or the private 1968 Reserve, a naturalist guide helps you spot toucans, coatis, and monkeys nesting in regenerating forests. Sweeping, panoramic vistas of Lake Arenal and the near-perfect volcanic cone reward you at the highest viewpoints.
location: Arenal 1968 Trailhead, La Fortuna
duration_note: Sturdy closed-toe hiking shoes with good traction are mandatory due to sharp volcanic rock surfaces.

name: Thermal Spring Hydrotherapy Ritual at EcoTermales Fortuna
description: You will unwind in elegant, naturally heated thermal pools tucked away inside an upscale, low-density rainforest reserve. Fed directly by mineral-rich springs flowing from the base of Arenal Volcano, these pools range from cool to a deeply relaxing 106°F. The lack of loud music or large crowds ensures a serene atmosphere surrounded by lit torches and tropical flora.
location: EcoTermales Fortuna, Route 142, La Fortuna
duration_note: Strictly limited capacity per entry session; booking weeks in advance is essential for evening slots.

name: Gravity-Defying Waterfall Canyoning & Rappelling
description: You will strap into a heavy-duty climbing harness and back over the edge of a roaring, 150-foot jungle waterfall. Drop down wet, sheer canyon walls into cold plunge pools, scramble over rugged river boulders, and finish with an adrenaline-pumping zipline drop. It is a fully immersive, soaking-wet adventure deep within a hidden tropical canyon.
location: Pure Trek Canyoning Canyon Base, La Fortuna
duration_note: Includes multi-terrain 4x4 transport and a hot Costa Rican lunch; requires a reasonable baseline of physical fitness.

name: Farm-to-Table Gastronomic Tasting at Don Rufino
description: You will experience the vanguard of contemporary Costa Rican cuisine at this legendary culinary landmark. Savor slow-roasted pork belly with local sweet potato puree, or wood-fired octopus brushed with regional chilies. The menu masterfully blends classic Tico comfort food roots with innovative, high-end international cooking techniques using ingredients sourced from neighboring valley farms.
location: Don Rufino, Center of La Fortuna, Alajuela
duration_note: A dress code of smart casual is expected; dinner reservations are highly advised, particularly between January and April.

name: Safari Float Wildlife Spotting by Inflatable Kayak
description: You will paddle down a calm, slow-moving jungle river while keeping your eyes peeled for nesting wildlife. Your guide will help you spot slow-moving sloths clinging to the canopy, curious howler monkeys, brightly colored iguanas sunning on river rocks, and rare tropical birds. The tranquil paddling allows you to take in the sounds of the active rainforest without motorized noise pollution.
location: Peñas Blancas River Putting-in, La Fortuna Area
duration_note: Excellent for families and photographers; dry bags are provided for camera gear; runs rain or shine.

name: Hanging Bridges Guided Canopy Walkway Tour
description: You will walk across a sophisticated trail network featuring 6 massive hanging bridges suspended high above the dense rainforest floor. Peer down into the green depths of the jungle canopy and enjoy stunning, unobstructed sightlines of Arenal Volcano. A certified naturalist guide spots incredibly camouflaged pit vipers, poison dart frogs, and sleeping bats that you would likely miss on your own.
location: Mistico Arenal Hanging Bridges Park, Route 142
duration_note: The trail is fully paved and highly accessible; early morning slots (6:00 AM - 8:00 AM) offer the best bird watching opportunities.

name: Local Craft Cocktails & Lounge Sessions at Vesta Gastronomy
description: You will dive into La Fortuna's elevated evening scene at this sleek, beautifully designed jungle lounge. Sip handcrafted signature cocktails featuring house-infused local rums, fresh passionfruit, and regional sugarcane syrups while listening to curated downtempo beats. It is the premier upscale spot to swap stories with global travelers after a long day of hiking.
location: Vesta Gastronomy & Cocktail Lounge, La Fortuna
duration_note: The lounge area is most active after 8:00 PM; look out for seasonal guest bartender events.

name: Extreme Canopy Ziplining & Mega Tarzan Swing at Selvatura
description: You will fly down Costa Rica’s most iconic zipline circuit, soaring across 13 cables suspended hundreds of feet over the misty cloud forest canopy. The absolute highlight is a 1-kilometer-long tandem cable where you zip 'Superman style' through the clouds, topped off by a massive, free-fall Tarzan Swing. It offers unmatched aerial thrills inside one of the world's most endangered forest ecosystems.
location: Selvatura Adventure Park, Monteverde
duration_note: Strict maximum weight limit of 280 lbs; the mountain air is noticeably cold and windy, so a windbreaker is highly recommended.

name: Resplendent Quetzal Guided Quest & Biological Trek
description: You will hike through a fairytale-like high-altitude ecosystem where moss-covered trees, orchids, and ferns are constantly bathed in a mystical, swirling fog. Using a high-powered spotting scope, an expert birding guide searches the wild avocado trees for the legendary, iridescent-green Resplendent Quetzal. You'll also cross a stunning continental divide bridge where the Caribbean and Pacific winds collide.
location: Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve Trailhead
duration_note: Park capacity is capped to protect wildlife; tickets must be purchased well ahead of time; peak Quetzal mating season runs March to June.

name: Night Wildlife Safari with Infrared Spotting
description: You will head into a private cloud forest reserve armed with a flashlight just as the sun sets and the jungle's nocturnal creatures wake up. Watch in awe as tarantulas emerge from ground burrows, green vipers coil on low branches, and sleeping toucans huddle in the canopy. If fortune smiles, you might even spot rare mammals like kinkajous, sloths, or an olingo moving through the dark.
location: Curi-Cancha Reserve, Monteverde
duration_note: Mandatory closed-toe shoes; heavy rain can impact wildlife activity, but tours still operate with provided ponchos.

name: From Tree to Cup: Organic Coffee & Cacao Workshop
description: You will walk through a family-run mountain plantation to harvest ripe, red coffee cherries right off the bush. Learn the traditional washing, drying, and roasting methods that give high-altitude Monteverde beans their distinct flavor profile. The workshop finishes with an interactive chocolate-making session, where you crush roasted cacao beans to create your own customized chocolate bars.
location: Don Juan Coffee & Chocolate Farm, Monteverde
duration_note: An excellent all-weather activity; price includes unlimited chocolate and coffee tastings throughout the tour.

name: Cloud Forest Yoga & Meditation Sound Bath
description: You will practice gentle Vinyasa flow on an open-air wooden platform looking out over the misty mountain canopy. The rustling wind, chirping frogs, and distant bird calls provide a soothing, natural soundtrack for your practice. The session ends with a deeply relaxing singing bowl sound bath designed to ground you after days of rigorous hiking and travel.
location: Monteverde Yoga Studio, Santa Elena
duration_note: All mats and props are provided; open to all experience levels; morning sessions are highly recommended before afternoon rains.

name: Microbrew Tastings & Live Music at Monteverde Beer House
description: You will head over to this beloved, rustic stone-and-wood pub to taste the mountain town's finest selection of locally brewed beers. Pull up a seat next to a mix of scientists, guides, and travelers to enjoy artisanal wood-fired pizzas and seasonal pub food. The warm atmosphere comes alive on weekends with local musicians playing folk, reggae, and acoustic rock.
location: Monteverde Beer House, Main Road, Santa Elena
duration_note: Arrive before 7:00 PM on live music nights to secure a table, as indoor seating is relatively limited.

name: World-Class Sunset Surf Academy on Playa Tamarindo
description: You will paddle out into the warm waters of Tamarindo's world-renowned beach break under the guidance of an ISA-certified surf coach. Learn proper pop-up techniques, ocean safety, and how to read the swells before catching your very first waves on a longboard. The session hits its peak just as the sky lights up with Guanacaste's legendary, fiery gold sunset.
location: Iguana Surf Beachfront HQ, Playa Tamarindo
duration_note: Includes rash guard and surfboard rental; lesson times shift daily to align perfectly with the tides.

name: Biodiverse Rainforest Trails & White Sand Coastal Walk
description: You will hike through a coastal rainforest where the jungle meet pristine, white-sand beaches. A naturalist guide uses a spotting scope to point out three-toed sloths, curious squirrel monkeys, and iguanas camouflaged along the trails. After your hike, reward yourself with a dip in the calm, turquoise waters of Playa Manuel Antonio inside the protected park reserve.
location: Manuel Antonio National Park Main Entrance, Quepos
duration_note: The park is strictly closed on Tuesdays; advance online passport-linked ticket registration via SINAC is mandatory weeks ahead; no single-use plastics allowed inside.

name: Ostional Wildlife Refuge Olive Ridley Turtle Nesting Night Safari
description: You will walk along a dark, protected beach under the stars to witness the incredible spectacle of an 'arribada'—where thousands of Olive Ridley sea turtles come ashore at once to nest. Witness these massive marine creatures dig their nests in the sand and lay their eggs before retreating back into the crashing surf. It is a profoundly moving, strictly regulated wildlife phenomenon.
location: Ostional National Wildlife Refuge Ranger Station
duration_note: Only accessible with a licensed local community guide; flash photography and white flashlights are strictly banned to prevent disorienting the turtles.

name: Oceanfront Wood-Fired Seafood Tasting at El Corazón
description: You will dine with your toes in the sand at this highly acclaimed open-air beachfront restaurant. Feast on fresh, day-boat yellowfin tuna seared over local hardwood, drizzled with lime-ginger glaze, and served alongside organic greens. The menu focuses heavily on line-caught, sustainable seafood delivered daily by local artisanal fishermen from the Nicoya Peninsula.
location: El Corazón Beachfront Bistro, Santa Teresa
duration_note: Prime sunset tables require booking weeks in advance during the high season; operations are subject to seasonal weather closures in October.

name: Beachfront Open-Air Party at El Vaquero & Crazy Monkey
description: You will dive straight into Tamarindo's legendary nightlife at this beachfront complex. Kick off the night with craft beers and live rock at El Vaquero, then head over to Crazy Monkey for high-energy fire shows, international DJs spinning electronic beats, and salsa dancing on the sand. It is a classic Costa Rican beach party where travelers and locals dance together late into the night.
location: El Vaquero Beachfront Stage, Playa Tamarindo
duration_note: Cover charges apply on big event nights; always stick to authorized taxis when heading home late from the beach venues.

name: Holistic Wellness & Vinyasa Intensive at Bodhi Tree Yoga Resort
description: You will find your center inside a stunning, open-air hardwood yoga shala nestled high up in the jungle canopy. Breathe deep to the soothing rhythm of ocean waves and cicadas while guided through an immersive chakra-balancing Vinyasa session. Afterward, refuel with a fresh, organic cold-pressed juice at the resort's clean-eating juice bar.
location: Bodhi Tree Yoga Resort, Nosara
duration_note: Drop-in classes are available daily, but it's best to check their online schedule beforehand as slots fill up fast.

name: Scuba Diving with Giant Pacific Manta Rays
description: You will board a custom dive boat and head out to volcanic rock formations renowned for incredible marine life encounters. Descend deep into blue waters to drift alongside majestic Giant Pacific Manta Rays boasting wingspans up to 20 feet. Along the way, you're likely to see schools of eagle rays, white-tip reef sharks, and sea turtles swimming through the volcanic rock arches.
location: Catalina Islands Diving Point, departure from Playas del Coco
duration_note: Requires an Open Water Certification; peak visibility and prime manta ray season runs from November through May.

name: Whale Watching & Whale Tail Coastal Sightseeing Tour
description: You will cruise through the waters of Uvita to witness magnificent Humpback Whales breaching and teaching their calves to swim. The boat skims past the famous 'Whale Tail'—a natural sand and rock formation that forms the shape of a perfect whale tail at low tide. Wrap up the journey by snorkeling over the largest coral reef on Costa Rica’s Pacific coast.
location: Marino Ballena Ranger Station, Uvita
duration_note: The prime whale migration seasons run from mid-July to October and again from January to March; park entry fee is included in the tour price.

name: Offshore Sportfishing Exploration for Sailfish & Marlin
description: You will set sail from the world-class Marina Pez Vela aboard a fully equipped 32-foot sportfishing vessel. Head out 20-30 miles into the deep blue waters of the Pacific, famous for holding massive concentrations of big-game pelagic fish. Under the guidance of an expert local crew, you'll try your hand at hooking and fighting world-record Sailfish, Marlin, and Dorado.
location: Marina Pez Vela, Quepos
duration_note: The price is for a private full-day boat charter for up to 5 anglers; strict catch-and-release policies apply to all billfish; includes all food, drinks, and top-tier gear.

name: ATV Backcountry Mountain Trails & Mud Track Adventure
description: You will power a heavy-duty 4x4 ATV up rugged, muddy mountain trails winding deep into the coastal ridge. Splash through shallow river crossings, navigate steep technical climbs, and stop at hidden jungle waterfalls for a refreshing swim. The ride rewards you with breathtaking, sweeping views overlooking the entire coastline of Jacó Beach.
location: Jacó Backcountry Base, Alajuela Road
duration_note: A valid driver's license is mandatory for all operators; prepare to get heavily covered in mud and dust; closed-toe shoes are required.

name: Deep Jungle Expedition to Sirena Ranger Station
description: You will trek deep into what National Geographic calls 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.' An expert naturalist guide leads you through old-growth primary rainforests to spot rare wildlife like Baird’s tapirs, herds of white-lipped peccaries, and all four of the country's native monkey species. The trail winds through dense wilderness before opening up to the remote, coastal Sirena outpost.
location: Sirena Ranger Station, Corcovado National Park (Access via Drake Bay)
duration_note: An ICT-licensed local guide is strictly mandatory to enter the park; day-trip permits are strictly limited and must be booked 3-6 months in advance.

name: Amazon-Style Waterways Exploration by Electric Canoe
description: You will glide quietly through a complex labyrinth of blackwater jungle canals inside a motorized, low-emission electric canoe. The silent motor allows you to sneak up close to river otters, caimans, basking iguanas, and rare birds like the Sungrebe. It is a completely peaceful, water-bound wilderness safari through a protected coastal wetland ecosystem.
location: Tortuguero National Park Main Canal Pier
duration_note: The park entrance ticket ($15 USD) must be purchased online prior to boarding; early morning 6:00 AM departures offer the absolute best wildlife viewings.

name: Surfing the Legendary 'Salsa Brava' Reef Break
description: You will test your skills against Costa Rica's most powerful, famous Caribbean reef break. Paddle out over a shallow, sharp coral reef to drop into a heavy, fast, and hollow right-hand barrel that draws expert surfers from across the globe. It is a high-intensity, thrilling ride reserved strictly for experienced, confident surfers.
location: Playa Cocles / Salsa Brava Reef, Puerto Viejo
duration_note: Strictly for expert surfers due to the shallow coral hazard; helm protection is highly advised; peak swell season runs from December through March.

name: Bribri Sacred Chocolate & Medicinal Plant Immersion
description: You will journey into the Talamanca mountains to visit an authentic, self-governed Bribri indigenous community. A tribal elder shares their deep spiritual connection to cacao, demonstrating traditional stone-grinding techniques used for ancient shamanic rituals. Afterward, you'll hike through their ancestral forest garden to learn how native plants are used to craft traditional medicines.
location: Bribri Reserve, Talamanca Valley (Pickup in Puerto Viejo)
duration_note: Requires deep respect for local cultural protocols; includes a traditional organic lunch wrapped in bijagua leaves.

name: Authentic Caribbean Rondon Stew Culinary Experience at Lidia's Place
description: You will sit down at a legendary, family-run Afro-Costa Rican spot to feast on true Caribbean Rondon (run-down) stew. Savor day-boat fish, crab, yuca, yams, and sweet plantains slow-simmered for hours in fresh, heavily seasoned coconut milk and spicy panamanian chilies. This meal beautifully showcases the distinct Afro-Caribbean roots that set this coast's culinary scene apart.
location: Lidia's Place, Calle Principal, Puerto Viejo de Talamanca
duration_note: Rondon is a slow-cooked dish that often requires advance phone ordering a few hours before dinner to guarantee availability.

name: Reggae Beats & Beachfront Nightlife at Johnny's Place
description: You will embrace the laid-back rhythm of the Caribbean coast at this iconic open-air beachfront bar. Sip cold Imperial beers and tropical rum cocktails while dancing on the sand to a lively mix of roots reggae, dancehall, and modern international beats. It is the premier late-night spot to gather around open beach bonfires and enjoy the warm Caribbean breeze.
location: Johnny's Place, Beachfront, Central Puerto Viejo
duration_note: The venue gets busiest after 10:00 PM; entry is typically restricted to adults 18 and older; casual beach attire is welcomed.

name: Coral Reef Snorkeling & Coastal Rainforest Hike
description: You will boat out to a protected marine sanctuary hosting one of Costa Rica's most expansive coral reef systems. Snorkel alongside schools of blue parrotfish, rock beauties, and sea turtles before heading ashore onto the national park's white-sand beaches. Finish with a coastal jungle hike where you'll look for white-faced capuchin monkeys, raccoons, and sloths.
location: Cahuita National Park Marine Pier, Cahuita
duration_note: Snorkeling over the reef is strictly forbidden without a certified local boat guide to protect the delicate coral structures.

name: Primary Jungle Trek to the Manzanillo Sea Cave Lookout
description: You will hike along an untamed coastal trail where primary rainforest meets dramatic, wave-sculpted black volcanic rock cliffs. The highlight is reaching the iconic Manzanillo Sea Cave and its natural rock arch, which frame a spectacular view of the crashing Caribbean sea. Your guide will help you spot green macaws soaring above and poison dart frogs hopping along the jungle floor.
location: Gandoca-Manzanillo National Wildlife Refuge Trailhead
duration_note: Trails can become incredibly muddy after rains; renting knee-high rubber boots at the entrance is highly recommended.

name: Bioluminescent Night Kayaking in the Inner Gulf
description: You will launch a kayak into the calm, pitch-black waters of the Golfo Dulce after the moon goes down. With every single stroke of your paddle, watch in awe as billions of microscopic dinoflagellates light up, casting an eerie, glowing blue trail through the water. Dip your hand in to watch the glowing water slip through your fingers while constellations shine bright above.
location: Golfo Dulce Launch Base, near Puerto Jiménez
duration_note: Best booked during the New Moon phase for peak darkness and visibility; all safety gear and glowing markers are provided.
